source.title: Is liquidity risk priced in cryptocurrency markets?
source.author: SeungOh Han

hypothesis: Cryptocurrencies with higher sensitivity to unexpected aggregate liquidity improvements earn higher subsequent weekly returns as compensation for systematic liquidity risk.
universe: Point-in-time Binance USD-M USDT perpetuals. Each Monday retain the top 50 contracts by lagged trailing-30-day quote volume with sufficient exact weekly history.
liquidity_measure: Daily Amihud proxy |close-to-close return| / quote_volume, averaged over the completed Monday-Sunday week. Weekly cross-sectional values are winsorized at 1%/99% before equal-weight aggregate illiquidity is formed.
aggregate_innovation: First difference of aggregate illiquidity is forecast causally with an expanding AR(1) using only earlier weeks; liquidity innovation is the negative one-step residual so positive values mean unexpectedly better market liquidity.
feature: Rolling beta = cov(asset weekly return, aggregate liquidity innovation) / var(aggregate liquidity innovation), using L prior completed weeks.
signal_direction: Long highest liquidity-beta quintile; short lowest quintile.
portfolio: Equal-weight market-neutral long/short, 0.5 gross per side.
execution: Beta estimate uses weeks completed before Monday rebalance. Enter Monday open and exit next Monday open.
development_gate: Canonical mean rank IC >0.02 with HAC p<0.05, positive high-minus-low weekly spread, canonical net Sharpe >0.70 and total return >0, and at least 2/3 beta windows positive after base costs.
success_gate: Canonical OOS net Sharpe >1.0; OOS rank IC >0.02; positive at 2x costs; at least 2/3 windows positive; 2024 and 2025 non-negative; max drawdown <35%; exclude BTC/ETH positive; exclude strongest contributor positive; DSR reported.
source_deviation: The paper scales aggregate liquidity changes by market capitalization and fits ARMA(1,2). Market cap is unavailable here. This preregistration instead uses lagged quote-volume eligibility and a causal expanding AR(1) innovation; the direction and beta-pricing hypothesis are unchanged.
